title: Manual entry: searchable typeahead over catalog, recency-ranked, last-quantity prefilled
goal: A household member can log a purchase without a receipt: search the catalog live, pick the item, confirm a prefilled quantity (and optional price), done in two taps for a repeat purchase -- or, when nothing matches, create a genuinely new catalog item through the same matching ladder S-09 already built, so manual entry never becomes a second, drifting source of duplicate catalog_items.
in_scope: Migration: search_catalog_items(p_household_id uuid, p_query text, p_limit int default 8) -- household-scoped, is_archived=false only. Empty query returns the top p_limit items ordered by item_stats.last_purchased_at desc nulls last (recency-ranked, REQ-07's default typeahead state before the user types anything). Non-empty query ranks by greatest(similarity(lower(canonical_name), p_query), max alias similarity, a 0.5 floor when canonical_name/brand ILIKE-contains p_query -- covers short queries under pg_trgm's practical floor, e.g. 2-3 char prefixes), filtered to score > 0.15, tie-broken by recency. Returns last_qty_base per item via coalesce(latest type='purchase' stock_movements.qty_base, catalog_items.default_pack_size, 1) -- same three-step fallback log_shopping_list_purchase already uses, so a first-ever manual purchase of a seeded-but-never-bought item still prefills something.

Migration: log_manual_purchase(p_household_id uuid, p_catalog_item_id uuid, p_new_item_name text, p_new_item_brand text, p_new_item_category_slug text, p_raw_text text, p_qty_base numeric, p_unit_price numeric, p_occurred_at timestamptz) returns table(out_catalog_item_id uuid, out_created_new boolean). Exactly one of p_catalog_item_id / p_new_item_name is non-null (existing-item path vs new-item path). Existing-item path: validates the id belongs to p_household_id and is not archived, raises otherwise. New-item path: resolves category by slug (same categories lookup + not-found guard as commit_receipt), inserts one catalog_items row (base_unit = category.default_base_unit, default_pack_size = null, is_staple = false) and one item_aliases row (source='manual', confidence=1.0, raw_text=p_raw_text). Both paths then: one stock_movements 'purchase' row at p_occurred_at (note='manual entry'), one price_history row when p_unit_price is not null, and the same item_stats upsert (purchase_count+1, last_purchased_at = greatest) commit_receipt/log_shopping_list_purchase already use. RETURNS TABLE columns are out_-prefixed per the S-24 ambiguous-column fix precedent.

lib/catalog/search.ts: searchCatalogItems(query) wrapping the RPC, household-scoped via getDefaultHouseholdId(); normalizes the query with canonicalize.ts's existing normalizeText() before it reaches SQL, so the same lowercase/whitespace-collapse rule governs both the trigram comparison and the eventual alias write.

lib/catalog/manual-entry.ts: logManualPurchase() for the existing-item path, and createNewItemAndLogPurchase() for the new-item path -- both call the RPC then recomputeOneItem(catalogItemId, householdId) exactly like logShoppingListPurchase's post-RPC call (no rateCorrectionOverride; S-15 reconciliation stays receipt-commit-only, unchanged invariant). createNewItemAndLogPurchase() first calls matchCatalogItem(supabase, householdId, normalizeText(name + brand)) (S-09's exact exported function, not reimplemented) as a duplicate safety net: if it resolves state='matched' (>=0.62), the function returns a typed 'likely_duplicate' result carrying the existing item's id/name instead of creating anything -- the caller surfaces 'This looks like an existing item: X -- select it instead' rather than silently creating a second catalog_items row for text the ladder already considers the same product. A 'needs_review' or 'new_item' result proceeds to create, since the user has already seen the live search results before choosing 'Add as new item' and this band is E-3's own definition of a legitimate ambiguous-but-proceedable case.

New-item quantity entry reuses normalizeUnitToBase() (S-10, already exported from lib/receipts/canonicalize.ts) exactly as the receipt commit path does: a qty + unit-display text field, converted against the resolved category's default_base_unit -- zero new unit-parsing logic. Existing-item quantity entry is a plain base-unit number field prefilled from last_qty_base (already in the item's base unit, no conversion needed).

app/add/manual/page.tsx + manual-entry-form.tsx ('use client'): debounced (~250ms) search input calling a searchCatalogAction server action via useTransition, rendering a ranked results list (name, brand, last purchased). Selecting a result shows a confirm card: quantity (prefilled, editable), optional price, 'Log purchase' button. When the query has no acceptable result, an 'Add "<query>" as a new item' affordance opens a small form (brand optional, category select from the seeded taxonomy, quantity + unit, optional price) wired to createNewItemAndLogPurchase(); a likely_duplicate result renders the suggested existing item instead of the form. Linked from app/add/capture.tsx ('Add manually' link) and app/page.tsx's Today card (alongside the existing /plan and /inventory links) as this repo's only current discovery surfaces for new routes.

Server Actions in app/add/manual/actions.ts: searchCatalogAction(query), logExistingItemPurchaseAction(catalogItemId, qtyBase, unitPrice), createNewItemPurchaseAction(FormData) -- revalidates '/', '/inventory', '/plan' on a successful write, matching lib/shopping-list/actions.ts's logPurchaseAction revalidation set (a manual purchase changes exactly the same downstream surfaces a shopping-list purchase does).
out_of_scope: The past-order override / backdating banner (REQ-22, S-27's territory) -- E-11's prd_ref is REQ-07/REQ-09 only. purchased_at defaults to now(); a manually backdated purchase stays correctly excluded from v_current_stock via the view's own occurred_at >= stock_epoch filter (no new code needed, same as S-27's finding for receipts) but there is no explicit override checkbox or 'items already at home' second movement for manual entry.

Re-deriving or persisting a top-3 candidate list server-side for the ambiguous band -- the live search results ARE the candidate list here (unlike a receipt's async review queue, the human is present at type-time), so there is nothing to persist.

Editing or deleting a manual purchase after logging -- matches commit_receipt's own out-of-scope precedent (ADR-0001, the ledger is the audit trail; a correction is a future adjustment movement, not a mutation).
Barcode scanning or any capture mechanism other than typed search -- REQ-07 is explicitly a typeahead.
acceptance: Repeating a common purchase takes two taps (REQ-07) -- verified as: tap a search result, tap 'Log purchase' with quantity already prefilled and price optional. A genuinely new item (no existing catalog match) can be created and logged through the same category taxonomy every other capture path uses, and a name that DOES resolve to an existing item via S-09's matching ladder is blocked from creating a duplicate and redirected to the existing item instead.
invariants: Never creates a second catalog_items row for text that matchCatalogItem resolves to an existing item at >=0.62 similarity -- the whole reason the new-item path calls into S-09's ladder rather than trusting the user's 'no match found' judgment alone.
base_unit for a newly created item comes only from the resolved category's default_base_unit, exactly as commit_receipt() already establishes for new_item receipt lines -- no ad hoc unit guessing.
All search/purchase RPC calls are household-scoped (ADR-0004); an archived item is never returned by search and never accepted as p_catalog_item_id by log_manual_purchase.

recomputeOneItem always runs after a successful log_manual_purchase call (existing or new item), same posture as every other purchase-writing path in this repo (S-13, S-24) -- a manual purchase that doesn't move the prediction is a silent correctness bug, not a missing feature.
